newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU Commission to fight Franco-German postal proposal.
newsitem.headline: EU Commission to fight Franco-German postal proposal.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it would do everything it could to stop France and Germany blocking plans to allow private firms to compete with European Union postal services.

Industry Commissioner Martin Bangemann told reporters the Commission had agreed at its weekly meeting that the Franco- German initiative, which would stop the EU from requiring any significant liberalisation before 2003, violated EU law.
"We cannot work on the basis of this compromise," he said.
The proposal, which will be discussed by EU telecommunications ministers on Thursday, has taken the Commission and other EU states by surprise.
France, wary of inciting unrest in its volatile public sector, has traditionally fought to delay opening up postal services to competition.
But Germany had taken a pro-liberalisation stance until earlier this month when it switched course and agreed to support France.
The central question is when to allow competition to provide direct mail and incoming cross-border mail.
Bangemann complained that the Franco-German initiative broke EU law by forbidding the Commission to use special treaty powers to enforce free-competition laws in the postal sector before 2003.
The EU treaty allows the Commission to adopt laws on its own to force national governments to open up public sectors to competition.
Bangemann said the proposal was also illegal because it called for EU ministers and the European Parliament to decide how to proceed after 1993 without a proposal from the Commission.
He noted that if ministers supported the Franco-German proposal, the Commission would have the right under EU law to withdraw its initial proposal and take the question off the table.
